$comment: The four component packs. "built" lists the components that have an implementation; "checks" records the quality gate results per component (unit, accessibility, visual, themes, responsive, parity). A component is Available only when every gate is passed. See docs/COMPONENT-PACKS.md. "next" is the version being built: the components it adds (planned until they pass their checks) and its notes.

packs.name: Premium Oracle JET
packs.frameworkRange: Oracle JET 6 and later, the release found in the bank’s code

builds.name: Classic JET
builds.builtOn: Classic oj-* elements wrapped in Knockout composites, using only the APIs JET 6 has (OBDX 22.1 ships JET 6.2).
builds.notes: The skin is plain CSS on the oj-* classes, so it needs no newer JET. elements gives the JET 6 element for each newer one the catalogue names (Core Pack oj-c-* elements, and oj-select-single from JET 8); own means a Knockout composite with no JET element under it.

builds.name: JET Core Pack
builds.builtOn: JET Core Pack oj-c-* elements wrapped in Knockout composites.
builds.notes: Assumed from JET 16, when the Core Pack elements the pack uses were all production. Change jetFrom here if a bank’s release proves otherwise.

packs.description: Every component as a drop-in for the bank’s JET UI: the Knockout bindings stay, only the element changes. The premium skin adds layered elevation, floating labels with a focus glow, gradient buttons that lift on hover, raised segments, status dots, tabular figures for money and 70 to 150 ms motion. The factory builds it for the JET release it finds when it scans the workspace’s code: classic oj-* elements up to JET 15, the JET Core Pack (oj-c-*) from JET 16.

dependencies.name: @oracle/oraclejet-core-pack
dependencies.version: the bank’s version, Core Pack build only
